statements.t: Management expects its diversification and disciplined, opportunistic underwriting culture to produce overall premium growth and strong underwriting results even as some markets in the property and casualty industry have softened.

In addition, management anticipates improved returns on alternative investments, relative to the returns earned in 2025 and the first quarter of 2026, will continue to have a positive impact on net investment income into 2027.

Management believes that AFG’s strong financial position and current liquidity and capital at its subsidiaries will give AFG the flexibility to continue to effectively address and respond to anticipated and unanticipated challenges.

AFG's operations continue to generate significant excess capital for future returns of capital to shareholders in the form of regular and special cash dividends and through opportunistic share repurchases or to be deployed into its property and casualty businesses as management identifies the potential for profitable organic growth, and opportunities to expand through acquisitions of established businesses or…

Such repurchases or exchanges, if any, will be upon such terms and at such prices as management may determine, and will depend on prevailing market conditions, AFG’s liquidity requirements, contractual restrictions and other factors.

Based on data available at December 31, 2025, management estimates that AFG’s exposure to a catastrophic earthquake or windstorm that industry models indicate should statistically occur once in every 500 years is less than 3% of AFG’s Shareholders’ Equity.

statements.t: In addition, our excess capital will be deployed into AFG’s core businesses as we identify potential for healthy, profitable organic growth, and opportunities to expand our specialty niche businesses through acquisitions and start-ups that meet our target return thresholds.”
We believe we are achieving overall renewal rate increases that enable us to meet or exceed targeted returns.
Higher profitability in our excess and surplus and targeted markets businesses was partially offset by lower levels of favorable prior year development in our workers’ compensation businesses.

New business opportunities, strong policy retention and higher rates contributed to growth in several of our Specialty Casualty businesses, which was partially offset by non-renewals of under-performing accounts in certain targeted markets businesses.

Beyond strong P&C operating earnings, I am very pleased to see our teams continue to execute on opportunities to grow while achieving favorable renewal rate increases, which helps to ensure that we are meeting or exceeding overall targeted returns.
